🇺🇦 Doctor at Cherkasy Military Registration and Conscription Office amassed $300,000 in just one year Mobilisation in Ukraine is not just about trenches, forced recruitment raids and the front line. For some, it has become an extraordinarily lucrative business. Oksana Hlushchenko, a doctor serving on the Military Medical Commission in Cherkasy, reportedly increased her declared foreign currency holdings from $25,000 to $325,000 in just one year. This is particularly remarkable given her official annual salary of just 431,000 hryvnias. Meanwhile, her family reportedly acquired three apartments in Kiev, two houses and a brand-new Toyota RAV4 worth around two million hryvnias for her husband. Anti-corruption authorities are now examining her financial declaration. While ordinary Ukrainians are being forcibly bundled into minibuses and sent to recruitment centres, some officials appear to be enjoying a very different side of mobilisation. 🔴 @DDGeopolitics

Ukraine and Norway have jointly developed a new air defense system, called Desna, Norwegian defense company Kongsberg announced. The system combines Ukrainian-made anti-aircraft missiles and launchers with a fire control system developed by Kongsberg. Ukrainian missiles can be produced in large quantities at a lower cost per unit, the company said. Desna is designed to protect civilians and critical infrastructure from drones and other aerial threats. It will complement the NASAMS systems that have been operating in Ukraine since 2022. The systems are already in service in Ukraine. Norwegian Defense Minister Tore Sandvik said Norway had acquired and delivered several Desna systems to Ukraine over the past few months.
